title: Africa: The Stars of the Moment in 2025
excerpt: From international hits and streaming records to prestigious nominations, African artists, athletes and creators are in the spotlight in 2025. Meet the top 10.
seo_title: Africa: The Stars of the Moment in 2025
seo_desc: Tyla, Ayra Starr, Tems, Burna Boy, Salah and more: the top 10 African stars of 2025 and why their global influence matters.
image_alt: Tyla, Ayra Starr, Tems and other African stars making waves in 2025
body_html:
Abidjan, 24 October 2025 – PRESS AFRICA – It is a rich year for African stars: amid international successes, streaming records, prestigious nominations and the expansion of their global influence, several artists, athletes and creators from the continent are taking centre stage. Here are three who embody this momentum.

Ayra Starr of Nigeria:

She is increasingly seen as "the Gen Z icon of Afrobeats". In 2025, she was the most-nominated African star at the 2025 BET Awards: three nominations, including "Best Female R&B/Pop", "Best New Artist" and "Best International Act", have put her under the global spotlight. Her album "The Year I Turned 21" dominated streaming platforms in West Africa in 2024-2025, and she is now engaged in international collaborations. Ayra Starr symbolises a new generation of African artists who are no longer content with the "local" but aim for the universal.

Tyla, the South African:

South African singer Tyla confirmed her global stature in 2025. After her hit "Water", she became the first South African artist to win a major prize at the iHeartRadio Music Awards (World Artist of the Year) and, at the American Music Awards, she took the title of "Favourite Afrobeats Artist". Tyla proves that African success is no longer confined to the continent: massive streaming, international tours, appearances at major festivals… She also embodies the growing power of Afrobeats in global pop culture.

Tems of Nigeria:

An already established artist, Tems continues to make her mark in 2025. She won a Grammy in the "Best African Music Performance" category for her track "Love Me JeJe" and consolidated her reputation as an influential voice of Afrobeats and African R&B. Beyond music, she is taking on a growing number of cross-disciplinary projects and is a link between African talent and global stages.

Why do these stars matter in 2025?

In terms of global reach: they go beyond Africa's borders, with international streaming, tours and collaborations with top artists. On the new generation and digital front, they make full use of digital platforms, TikTok and Instagram, and are redefining African identity in global pop. Beyond music, they are brands, creators and role models for young people on the continent in the fields of image and influence. Their track records are also diverse: although all three are musicians, they show that Africa no longer has a single "type" of success but several avenues (fashion, multimedia, international collaboration).

The influence of these celebrities also raises important questions. What about the management of their image, the capture of value for their home countries, their social impact? The role of African stars is evolving. They are no longer merely "representatives" but potentially agents of change.

The Top 10 African stars in 2025

1. Tyla (South Africa) – Global singer of the year: after her worldwide hit "Water", Tyla consolidated her fame with a sold-out world tour and a historic win at the 2025 American Music Awards. She has become a global ambassador for African pop and the amapiano style, inspiring an entire generation of young artists.

2. Ayra Starr (Nigeria) – Gen Z icon of Afrobeats: three nominations at the 2025 BET Awards and collaborations with American stars (SZA, Chris Brown). She embodies the feminisation of African musical leadership and Nigeria's cultural power on the world stage.

3. Tems (Nigeria) – Golden voice and symbol of excellence: 2025 Grammy winner for "Best African Music Performance" with Love Me JeJe. She is stepping up charitable initiatives in West Africa and promotes an image of authenticity and female empowerment.

4. Burna Boy (Nigeria) – Ambassador of the continent: in 2025, he celebrated passing the billion-stream mark on Spotify and remains one of the highest-paid African artists in the world. He has also launched a foundation for African youth, focused on culture and entrepreneurship.

5. Asisat Oshoala (Nigeria) – Icon of African women's football: the Nigerian striker, a star of FC Barcelona Femení, won her sixth African Women's Player of the Year award. She is an active campaigner for the recognition and funding of women's sport on the continent.

6. Wizkid (Nigeria) – The musical strategist: still a headliner, Wizkid released a critically acclaimed album with hybrid Afro-Latin sounds in 2025. He remains an essential reference in the global Afrobeats industry.

7. Black Sherif (Ghana) – The African hip-hop revelation: with his album The Villain I Never Was II, he has conquered the English-speaking African market and performed on Europe's biggest stages. He symbolises the rise of conscious African hip-hop, rooted in the continent's social reality.

8. Trevor Noah (South Africa) – Voice of African humour and lucidity: the former host of The Daily Show continues an international stand-up career, with his Born a Lion tour in 2025. He remains an emblematic figure of an unapologetic African voice facing the West.

9. Angelique Kidjo (Benin) – The eternal legend: in 2025, she celebrated 40 years of career with a monumental concert in Cotonou and a world tour, "Mother of Sound". Still committed, she champions the cause of girls and education in Africa through her Batonga Foundation.

10. Mohamed Salah (Egypt) – The pharaoh of football: a star of Liverpool FC, Salah remains a model of humility and sporting excellence. In 2025, he passed the 250-goal mark in his European career, consolidating his status as a living legend of African sport.

These ten personalities embody a modern, bold and creative Africa, proud of its roots but turned towards the world. Their success is no longer limited to the continent's borders: they shape global trends, redefine the image of Africa and inspire a new generation.

Writer: Jaurès BOKO
